statement: CoreWeave's live pricing page lists on-demand rates including $49.24/hour for an 8-GPU HGX H100 node and $68.80/hour for an 8-GPU HGX B200 node, while its newest GB300 NVL72 and HGX B300 systems show no public rate and are quoted only via sales.
why: A named neocloud's published rate card is the cleanest read on what current-generation capacity actually costs, and the newest parts being sales-quoted only suggests they are not freely available on demand.

impact.mechanism: Published node rates set the observable rental level for deployed accelerators; withheld pricing on the newest systems is a display-level observation about availability rather than a scored demand signal.

evidence.excerpt: NVIDIA HGX H100, '8 GPU Count, 80 VRAM (GB)' at $49.24/hour on-demand
NVIDIA HGX B200, '8 GPU Count, 180 VRAM (GB)' at $68.80/hour on-demand
NVIDIA GB300 NVL72, '4 GPUs, 279GB VRAM', pricing 'Contact sales' (no on-demand rate shown)

confidence.basis: Vendor's own live rate card but carried at secondary tier with no last-updated date on the page, and no stated prior level to compare against.

dispersion: A third-party normalization published 2026-07-01 cites $21.60/hr for an 8-GPU H100 node against the $49.24/hour shown live, indicating stale outside figures circulate alongside the current page.
